calls.reason: Microsoft's hardware spending and Amazon's Anthropic investment show substantial commitments, but neither establishes who uses most capacity or whether both labs require continual funding.
Microsoft reports a $37 billion AI revenue run rate, but the packet establishes neither cumulative AI spending nor comparable returns. Calling those revenues pathetic is an opinion.
The Next Web reports an annual revenue concentration estimate near 70%, supporting that component. Neither that report nor the Azure hosting agreement establishes majority infrastructure use.
Semafor documents different gross-versus-net revenue presentations, but does not establish misleading annualization by both labs or rule out a route to profitability.
Cursor's announcement and SpaceX's filing confirm an August acquisition. They do not establish the predicted Musk–Truell falling-out or a rushed sale caused by it.

Oracle's substantial AI contracts challenge the exclusivity claim. Microsoft and Amazon disclose revenue run rates, but the packet lacks verified cumulative spending needed to assess the ratios and settle the main point.
